scope: Original-XML topology and synthetic graph verification only; no current pedestrian permission, shop entrance, physical walkability or global shortest-path claim.

checks.name: Original XML hash matches source manifest and network provenance
Every network node preserves XML ID, coordinates and node tags
Every network way preserves full XML node order and tags
Sample uses original road nodes, leaves POIs unconnected and ineligible
Every sample edge follows adjacent original way nodes and exact XML coordinates
Sample edge and total distances match independent Haversine oracle
Sample source ways have no bridge, tunnel, nonzero layer, steps or explicit foot prohibition
Geometric intersection alone does not connect; a shared original node does
Missing source nodes break connectivity while complete remaining segments survive
Motor-vehicle one-way does not constrain walking; oneway:foot does
Way foot prohibition wins; explicit foot permission overrides general restricted access
Directional private foot access excludes only that direction
Ground-only model excludes bridges, tunnels and nonzero layers
Barrier nodes block gates without permission and honor explicit foot permission/prohibition
Unreachable and unknown endpoints return null
Shortest path chooses the shorter connected alternative rather than an arbitrary detour
Explicit foot-restriction exclusion list is enforced
Pedestrian-only and avoid-steps options exclude their distinct road classes

limitations: Tests establish consistency with retained source records and graph rules, not current real-world permission or physical access.
The retrieval rectangle does not guarantee complete surrounding connectivity or a global shortest route.
Sample endpoints are road nodes; candidate POI entrances remain unverified and disconnected.
